name: tier1_floor_traverse_chokepoint
_comment: RULED (Rafe, 2026-08-29), overturning Ruling 70's execution by §13.9's own second consequence:
the closure named the WRONG ILLUMINATION. The path signal is keyed to where the player walks,
and the player CARRIES THE LAMP - so a static scene-wide capture measures the signal precisely
where its reader never is. Measured on the capture that closed the channel: the tiles the
traffic field calls busiest sat at illumination 7.1/255, and the whole nine-rung palette
rendered there into four 8-bit values. That is a true finding about scene-dark delivery and it
is retained as bible §13.9. It is not a finding about the path.
So the population is corrected. The player STANDS ON THE ROUTE and the route lies inside the
lamp's delivered pool, which is the only condition under which the question 'does the floor
know where it goes' was ever going to be answerable.
DESIGN RULING recorded with it: the path is built for LIT LEGIBILITY. Player-as-light-source is
the normal case, some corridors will carry fixed light later (orc fires), and DARK ILLEGIBILITY
IS ACCEPTED BY DESIGN. A floor is not required to state its route into the dark.
Geometry, carve list and mocked walls are IDENTICAL to tier1_floor_review.json - only the
player's station moves, so every comparison through that spec stays valid.
THIS STATION: mid-chokepoint, one tile wide, polished wall to wall because the traffic had no room to spread. The route runs both ways out of the pool.
_legibility: Derived from the ratified rig (Ruling 56, radius 5.0 tiles) and the sweep recorded in
tier1_floor_review.json: two tiles delivers ~0.66 and anything past five is ambient.
The lit point is ON THE ROUTE inside the pool; the dark point is on the same route
beyond the lamp, which is the condition the design ruling accepts rather than fights.

A point at 7 tiles lands at py 1026 against a view that ends at 1001 and the probe REFUSED the capture rather than measuring the letterbox - the same class of mistake the parent spec records at its own two tries. Six tiles is the furthest declarable dark.

legibility.why: on the route, 2 tiles - inside the delivered pool, where the reader stands
the same route at 6 tiles - past the lamp's delivered reach and still inside the dungeon view; dark illegibility accepted by design
